newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares close at record above 4,000 points.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares close at record above 4,000 points.

text.p: The Swiss bourse closed firmer across a broad front on Thursday as the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) finished above 4,000 points for the first time.
Technical factors, favourable bond markets, firming European bourses and strong advances in Roche certificates and major banks powered the rise, dealers said. Volume was high.

"We had a very active day and we remain very optimistic for the next two weeks," one trader said, but added by month's end investors may turn wary ahead of February's U.S. Federal Reserve FOMC meeting.
The SMI rose 0.69 percent, or 27.5 points, to 4,007.1 after coming off a new intra-day high of 4,009.2 points.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) advanced 17.10 points, or 0.67 percent, to 2,568.85 points.
Dealers said some of the moves were incidental as investors squared positions ahead of Friday's expiry on options and futures exchange Soffex.

Roche certificates, which led the active list, powered ahead 135 francs to close at an all-time high of 10,985 Swiss francs. The company reported 1996 sales rose 11 percent to 15.96 billion francs, beating market expectations of around 15.8 billion.

Banks, which have been under pressure recently due to a row about dormant accounts of Holocaust victims, gained ground on easing tensions between Switzerland and Jewish organisations. CS Group stood out with a jump of 3.50 francs, or 2.61 percent, to 137.75 francs.

UBS bearer shares added nine francs to 1,155. After the bourse close, Standard & Poor's said it downgraded UBS's long-term rating to double-A-plus from triple-A. UBS has been on S&P's CreditWatch list since November after forecasting a loss of around 500 million francs due to extraordinary provisions.
